statement: Let M = 1000000007 and S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |nums1[k] - nums2[k]|. For 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, let C(i,j) = S - |nums1[i] - nums2[i]| + |nums1[j] - nums2[i]|. Let B be the minimum of S and all values C(i,j); this is the true absolute sum difference after either no replacement or one replacement of nums1[i] by the value nums1[j]. The function returns a result r such that 0 <= r < M and there is an integer q >= 0 with B = q * M + r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (overflow, out-of-bounds, or panic) on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r < 1000000007.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |nums1[k] - nums2[k]|, let B be the true minimum absolute sum difference after at most one replacement, and let D = max_{0 <= i < n} |nums1[i] - nums2[i]|. Whenever the function returns r, r is B modulo 1000000007 and S - D <= B <= S.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.
Let n = len(nums1). Assume n = 1, len(nums2) = 1, and 1 <= nums1[0] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[0] <= 100000.
Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000 for every i, and nums1[i] = nums2[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |c - nums2[k]|. The function returns r such that 0 <= r < 1000000007 and S = q * 1000000007 + r for some integer q >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000 for every i. Assume also that there is an integer c with nums1[i] = c for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |nums1[k] - c|, Dmax = max_{0 <= i < n} |nums1[i] - c|, and Dmin = min_{0 <= j < n} |nums1[j] - c|. The function returns r such that 0 <= r < 1000000007 and S - Dmax + Dmin = q * 1000000007 + r for some integer q >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000 for every i. Assume also that there is an integer c with nums2[i] = c for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |nums1[k] - nums2[k]|, and for 0 <= i,j < n let C(i,j) = S - |nums1[i] - nums2[i]| + |nums1[j] - nums2[i]|. Let B be the minimum of S and all C(i,j). Whenever the function returns r, there exist indices i,j with 0 <= i,j < n such that C(i,j) = B, and r is B modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let S = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |nums1[k] - nums2[k]|, for 0 <= i,j < n let C(i,j) = S - |nums1[i] - nums2[i]| + |nums1[j] - nums2[i]|, and let B be the true minimum after at most one replacement. Whenever the function returns r, r is B modulo 1000000007, B <= S, and B <= C(i,j) for every 0 <= i,j < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every permutation pi of {0,1,...,n-1}, define slices a' and b' of length n by a'[i] = nums1[pi(i)] and b'[i] = nums2[pi(i)] for 0 <= i < n. Whenever min_absolute_sum_diff(nums1, nums2) returns r and min_absolute_sum_diff(a', b') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: For any integer c such that 1 <= nums1[i] + c <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] + c <= 100000 for all 0 <= i < n, define a'[i] = nums1[i] + c and b'[i] = nums2[i] + c. Whenever min_absolute_sum_diff(nums1, nums2) returns r and min_absolute_sum_diff(a', b') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.
